github_issue.notes: Every load-bearing claim verified against the repo: exactly 11 `sed -i ... 2>/dev/null || true` sites at build_and_run.sh:347-348/366-367/388-389/411-412/433-434/654, GNU-only `stat -c '%U'` at line 248, clean-keycloak.sh:158-159, and terraform/telemetry-collector/deploy.sh already using `sed -i.bak`. Acceptance criteria are genuinely testable (exactly one SECRET_KEY line, inode/permissions preserved, abort on unwritable .env, operator values untouched) and the out-of-scope section names real sibling code with reasons. Strongest aspect is the precise root cause (BSD sed -i suffix parsing plus bash last-wins vs compose first-wins divergence), corroborated by docker-compose.yml:129/230 `${OPENBAO_TOKEN:?}` and auth_server/internal_request_token.py:69 raising on missing SECRET_KEY. The only unverifiable claim is the external issue #1577 reference; risk coverage is solid but deliberately thin, deferring depth to the design.

lld.notes: The design commits to every decision an implementer needs: full helper source, exact call-site replacements with per-hunk line targets, error/logging contract, and a alternatives matrix with honest rejections (sed -i.bak leaves secret-bearing backups). Repo grounding checks out precisely: line refs 347/366/388/411/433/654 match the file, `set -e` is line 4, validate-extra-env.sh is sourced at line 582, and no pre-existing EXIT trap exists so the helper's trap is safe. Largest deficiencies are small: the claim that the helper returns nonzero 'without touching <file>' overstates the mid-write truncation edge, the LOC table is off (~22 vs the actual 46-line helper, '11 replaced by 5' vs 6 calls), and the rejected grep -v alternative misstates its exit-code semantics. Risk handling of the temp-file secret copy, inode preservation, and the delete-any-value precondition is genuinely thorough for a trivial-complexity change.

review.notes: This is a real review, not praise: it surfaces concrete defects in its own design (empty-name call degenerating to `/^=/d`, the silent-failure shape without helper self-diagnostics, non-structural temp cleanup on kill -9) and the claimed resolutions verifiably appear in the revised LLD Step 1 and in the patch. Technical claims check out: handle_error ends at build_and_run.sh:15, no other EXIT trap exists, and the double-vs-single-quoted trap reasoning about losing the function-local $tmp is correct. Largest gaps: no reviewer catches that the final helper comment contains the literal string 'sed -i', which invalidates the testing plan's 1.4 oracle, and the frontend section adds essentially nothing. Verdicts are differentiated and findings are prioritized into consolidated blocking items with resolutions.

testing.notes: Cases A-F carry real oracles (grep -c exactly 1, inode comparison via ls -i, byte-identical diff), the unwritable-file negative case exercises the helper's actual failure path, and rollback/backward-compat sections are proportionate; extraction anchors agree with the repo (`# Generate a random SECRET_KEY` at build_and_run.sh:341). Two oracles fail as written against the submitted patch: section 1.4 expects `grep -n "sed -i"` to return nothing, but the shipped helper comment literally contains 'sed -i' (implementation.md itself admits the comment match — a cross-artifact inconsistency), and the 1.2 block harness never sources `log`/`handle_error`, so its 'log line SECRET_KEY added to .env present' expectation cannot hold. The chmod 444 negative case would also false-pass under a root-running CI runner. Coverage of the acceptance criteria is otherwise complete, with honest non-execution disclosure and no CI automation offered.

implementation.notes: `git apply --check` against the 1.27.1 checkout (commit 5f725c1d1d1a3515840b17e29a2b7f22a0c1fd09 verified) exits 0, every hunk's context matches the real file including the metrics-loop guard at line 650, and the working tree was left untouched. The patch implements the revised LLD end to end: all 11 silenced sed sites replaced by 6 loud helper calls aborting through handle_error, helper placement after line 15 before all call sites, and the summary's +60/-17 arithmetic is exact. Largest residual risk is the widened delete-any-value semantics (a populated line coexisting with an empty placeholder is now regenerated rather than preserved), a contrived state the code comments and LLD explicitly analyze. Tests were not executed and the summary says so plainly, listing deliberately excluded follow-ups (clean-keycloak.sh, stat -c, CI guard) rather than overselling.

verdict: An exceptionally well-grounded, internally consistent artifact set whose verified patch applies cleanly to the real source, with the largest material limitation being the testing plan's two oracles that fail as written against the shipped patch (the 'sed -i' grep that matches the helper's own comment and the end-to-end harness that never sources log/handle_error).
